title: Add CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards + warmup; fix regression
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Fixes regression in CUDA graph warmup and adds robust shape-guarded graph capture/replay path. Improves inference tail latency and reduces per-token cost under steady workloads.
description: Context: recent work to introduce CUDA Graph capture/replay yielded measurable throughput improvements but introduced a warmup regression in scenarios with variable sequence lengths (ENG-1124). This PR implements shape guards for graph capture to ensure correctness across variable-length requests, adds an explicit warmup path that primes KV cache and persistent graph state, and includes a number of safety checks and fallbacks to the baseline kernel path. Changes include: 1) Graph manager updates to record and compare shape signatures before reuse; 2) Warmup API that schedules a lightweight synthetic request to populate KV caches and create graphs ahead of traffic; 3) Scheduler tweaks to prefer graph-backed execution for stable shapes and fall back when a shape mismatch is detected; 4) Tests and perf harness updates and documentation for ops teams. Motivation: address reported regressions where cold-start latency regressed and some requests hit incorrect graph replays leading to corrupted KV lookups. This PR fixes the regression while preserving the throughput benefits for stable workloads. Testing: unit tests for ShapeSignature, integration tests exercising shape mismatch and fallback, end-to-end perf canary with synthetic and replayed traffic (results included below). Checklist: - [x] Implement shape signature and guard logic - [x] Add warmup priming API + opt-in config - [x] Scheduler fallback and telemetry hooks - [x] Add unit & integration tests - [x] Performance canary run and result validation - [x] Documentation and runbook notes for on-call. Notes: the change intentionally keeps graph capture opt-in behind a feature flag set via deployment config to allow staged rollout. We observed ~18% token-per-second improvement on A100 under pinned-shape workloads and no regression on mixed-shape workloads after warmup and guard logic. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.

ci_checks: perf-canary: passed (18% tps improvement on A100 for pinned shapes)
perf_summary: Pinned-shape workload (A100): baseline 12.4k tokens/s -> graph-backed 14.6k tokens/s (+17.7%)
Mixed-shape workload (A100): baseline 9.1k tokens/s -> graph-enabled with warmup 9.0k tokens/s (no regression)
Cold-start 99th percentile latency reduced from 360ms -> 260ms after warmup priming
testing_notes: Added unit tests covering ShapeSignature equality and mismatch fallback
Integration test simulates shape mismatch and asserts correct fallback and KV cache integrity
Canary run included production-like replay trace and synthetic priming requests
merge_summary: Squash merged by Ben Chu. Rationale: fixes regression and adds feature guarded graph capture/replay with warmup priming; opt-in feature flag for controlled rollout. All CI green and reviewers approved.
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag in canary region and measure fallback metrics for 48 hours before wider rollout. If fallback_rate > 0.5% escalate to infra on-call.
incident_link: SUP-4421: customer reported cold-start regression in dedicated cluster
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: graph reuse across mismatched shapes could silently corrupt KV state. Mitigation: strict shape guards, telemetry, and immediate fallback to kernel path plus runbook to roll back feature flag.
notes: This PR should be tracked in the rollout dashboard (ENG-1198) and included in the next runtime release notes with a short explanation of the feature flag and recommended canary steps.
